prompt: Draw a pelican riding a bicycle along a beach, as a single self-contained SVG. Side view. The pelican sits on the saddle, its feet on the pedals and a wing on the handlebars. Behind it: sea meeting sand, sky above. It must read unmistakably as a PELICAN (long straight bill with a hanging throat pouch) on an unmistakable BICYCLE (two equal spoked wheels, a diamond frame between them).
definition_of_done: final_output_file: pelican.svg, a single self-contained SVG. All 11 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. The file parses as XML, has a viewBox of 4 numbers at least 100x100, contains no <script>, <image> or <foreignObject>, and makes zero external requests (no http(s) href/src, no @import, no url(//...)). It carries elements with exactly these ids: beach, sea, sand, bicycle, wheel-rear, wheel-front, frame, pelican, bill, pouch, eye. Measured geometry, not vibes: the two wheel rim circles match in radius within 2%, their centres are level within 5% of the radius, they do not overlap, and the wheelbase is 2.0-6.0 times the wheel radius. The eye sits above the top of the rear wheel. bill and pouch are separate elements. The sea renders above the sand. If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a partial drawing or a file that dodges the tests.
contract: Produce ONE SVG document in the `code` field, starting with <svg and ending with </svg>. Root <svg> needs xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" and a viewBox. Tag the semantic parts with these exact ids so the drawing is inspectable: beach (the whole background scene), sea, sand, bicycle, wheel-rear, wheel-front, frame, pelican, bill, pouch, eye. Each wheel group contains a <circle> for its rim, with numeric cx, cy and r; the largest circle in the group is taken as the rim, so hubs and spoke dots may be smaller circles in the same group. Both rims share a radius and a cy. The eye is a <circle> (or an element with a numeric y) positioned above the wheels. bill and pouch must be two different elements, not one shape doing both jobs. Everything inline: no external fonts, no raster images, no scripts, no network. Gradients, paths and groups are all fine.
